Umbrasas / LRT Farms across Lithuania are relying increasingly on foreign workers, and farmers expect the trend to continue for years to come. The country's Vegetable Growers' Association says almost all farms are struggling to find staff, particularly for short-term work, driving a rise in the use of foreign labour-hire agencies.Â According to Lithuania's Employment Service, more than 5,000 foreigners are now employed on the country's farms, with the majority coming from outside the EU, though numbers from within the bloc are also rising. At one farm in the Kaunas district, a third of the workforce comes from Ukraine. Olha, one of the farm's Ukrainian workers, moved to Lithuania to be with her son, Andriy. "I came to look after my granddaughter. After a month I decided to go out and work [...] We make meat rolls, sausages, we do all sorts of jobs in the workshop â if they need help in the dairy, we go there," she told LRT. "[The farm owner] took us on, we work, the pay is good, the conditions are decent," said Andriy. Farming (associative) | D. Umbrasas / LRT The farm's owner, Audrius Banionis, said he had previously employed workers from Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Mozambique. ' "You could write jokes about their work," he said, adding that he found it a bit easier to reach an understanding with Ukrainian workers. "Just like Lithuanians, there are all sorts foreigners â some who drink, some who eat well, some who are lazy, some who wander off. It's the same with Ukrainians, but as a workforce, I'd say they're probably more culturally close to us," he said. Banionis said he had bought flats and houses to accommodate his foreign workers, and also tries to look after their free time. "You wouldn't believe it, we dance and sing with them, but we try to help them settle in," he said. According to Paulius Andriejavas, chairman of the Vegetable Growers' Association, almost every farm is short of workers, with the problem particularly acute when extra hands are needed for short periods, such as during harvest. "We have a few hired workers, they're from Africa, from Pakistan, but we're trying it out, taking the first steps, and we'll see how it goes," he said, adding that only around two in ten foreign workers meet expectations. "Farms aren't places any more where work can be done just any old way. There are requirements for packaging, for product quality, for how goods are prepared. The standards are high," he said. Farmers expect the number of foreign workers to keep rising over the next five years, as fewer Lithuanians are willing to take on such jobs. "What's most in demand is livestock work â as a rule, in Lithuania, especially around towns and cities, no Lithuanian wants to go near it, there's manure and so on," said Mindaugas MaciuleviÄius, head of the Kaunas branch of the Farmers' Union. Farming (associative) | D. Umbrasas / LRT As agriculture becomes more mechanised, farms are increasingly short of skilled workers too. "Around 20% are doing unskilled work, roughly speaking, all the rest are people with particular specialisms needed in our agriculture sector. That means, above all, operators of agricultural machinery, so drivers of tractors, combine harvesters and other specialised equipment, and another group is heavy goods vehicle drivers," said Jurgita ZemblytÄ, head of the Employment Service's monitoring and analysis division. The Employment Service said most vacancies were in farms in the Pakruojis, RadviliÅ¡kis and PanevÄÅ¾ys districts, with the highest wages on offer for agricultural machinery drivers and the lowest in crop-growing operations. https://www.naturalnews.com/2026-08-14-u.text: The MQ-9 Reaper is used for surveillance and airstrikes, and the report noted the aircraft is "extremely vulnerable" when used against an enemy with air defenses [1] . The drones were deployed extensively over the decades for strikes in the U.S. War on Terror, which continues in Somalia, according to the report [1] . Earlier reporting by Bloomberg, summarized by NaturalNews.com in May, estimated that Iran had destroyed approximately $1 billion worth of MQ-9 Reapers, representing about 20 percent of the Pentagon's prewar inventory of unmanned aerial vehicles [2] . Reported Causes of Drone Losses According to The Washington Post, the 45 MQ-9s were lost through a combination of shootdowns by Iran, strikes by Iranian missiles and drones at U.S. bases in the region, and crashes caused by communications errors [1] . A fourth U.S. official told the newspaper that not all of the lost drones were shot down; some crashed after losing communications with their operators, according to RT's summary of the report [3] . The report also stated that the U.S. lost more than 20 MQ-9s during bombing campaigns against Ansar Allah, the Houthi movement in Yemen, in 2024 and 2025 [1] . Houthi forces claimed responsibility for downing a U.S. MQ-9 near Yemen in February 2024, an aircraft with a price tag of $32 million, according to reporting by NaturalNews.com [4] . Communications failures have been documented in other MQ-9 incidents. In March 2024, an MQ-9 made an emergency landing in Poland after losing connection with its command station, according to the Pentagon [5] . Replacement Cost Estimate Replacing the 45 lost aircraft could cost up to $2.25 billion, according to the Post report [1] . RT, reporting on the same story, put the cost to U.S. taxpayers at an estimated $1.3 billion [3] . The losses add to the overall cost of the U.S. campaign in Iran. Operation Epic Fury, launched by President Donald J. Trump on February 28, 2026, cost between $22.3 billion and $31 billion over its first five weeks, according to research from the American Enterprise Institute cited by NaturalNews.com [6] . Separately, defense contracting has a documented record of price escalation; author David Dayen's book "Monopolized" describes how supplier TransDigm raised prices on military parts year after year [7] . Military Value and Official Assessment Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Kenneth S. Wilsbach called the MQ-9 the "most valuable player" of the U.S.-Israeli bombing campaign, according to his testimony to Congress [1] . "No other platform is even close to the MQ-9" in terms of the number of strikes launched in Iran, Wilsbach told Congress on Wednesday [1] . "It's an unmanned platform, so we get a lot of utility out of them, and don't put our folks at risk," Wilsbach said [1] . The report noted that the bombing campaign has killed more than 3,400 Iranians, around half of whom were civilians [1] . The MQ-9's predecessor, the MQ-1 Predator, was used as a "judge-jury-and-executioner assassination weapon" in Yemen as early as 2002, according to Nick Turse's book "The Complex" [8] . Armed remotely piloted aircraft have since become a central feature of U.S. military operations, the book documents [8] . Regional Outlook U.S. MQ-9 operations over the Strait of Hormuz are continuing despite the losses, according to the report [1] . On August 3, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it shot down another MQ-9 in the area, according to the report [1] . The possibility of renewed U.S. strikes in Iran remains, according to the report, as long as the U.S. continues enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports and maintains a ramped-up deployment in the region [1] . U.S. officials have said the naval blockade could be lifted once a deal on the Strait of Hormuz is finalized, according to Zero Hedge [9] . References Dave DeCamp. https://telex.hu/eszkombajn/2026/09/30/h.text: Menü Kereső Ha a Naprendszer tele van menő holdnevekkel, a Földét miért simán csak úgy hívják, hogy Hold? Észkombájn Az amerikai űrkutatási hivatal, a NASA által közreadott felvétel a Hold mögött elhaladó Föld bolygóról, amelyet az Artemis II küldetésben részt vevő űrhajósok örökítettek meg 2026. április 6-án – Fotó: NASA Dévai László Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A Naprendszer tele van jól hangzó nevű holdakkal. A Jupiter körül kering például az Io, az Europa, a Ganymedes és a Callisto, a Szaturnusznak pedig ott van többek között a Titan, a Rhea vagy az Enceladus. Ehhez képest a Föld egyetlen természetes kísérőjét egyszerűen csak Holdnak, angolul Moonnak hívjuk. Mintha az emberiség elnevezett volna minden más égitestet, a hozzánk legközelebbiről viszont megfeledkezett volna. Valójában éppen fordítva történt. A Holdnak azért nincs olyan tulajdonneve, mint az Iónak vagy az Europának, mert amikor az emberek nevet adtak neki, még nem tudták, hogy léteznek más holdak is. Évezredeken keresztül nem egy volt a sok hasonló égitest közül, hanem az egyetlen ilyen objektum, amit az ember ismert. Az angol moon szó egészen az óangol mōna alakig vezethető vissza. Eredete az idő mérésével és a hónapokkal függ össze, ami nem meglepő: az emberek jóval a modern naptárak megjelenése előtt is használták a Hold szabályosan ismétlődő fázisait az idő múlásának követésére. A szó eredete kapcsolatban áll a latin metri, vagyis mérni és mensis, vagyis hónap szavakkal is. Ugyanebből a régi kapcsolatból érthető meg az angol moon és month közötti rokonság is. Vagyis a Hold nem azért lett Moon, mert valaki egyszer tulajdonnevet adott neki. A megnevezés összefonódott azzal, ahogyan az emberek az égitest mozgását és változásait megfigyelve az időt mérték. Ez évszázadokon át nem is okozott különösebb problémát. Aztán 1610-ben Galileo Galilei az ég felé fordította távcsövét, és a Jupiter mellett négy kisebb égitestet figyelt meg. Ma ezeket Iónak, Europának, Ganymedesnek és Callistónak nevezzük, és a Jupiter négy legnagyobb holdjaként ismerjük őket. A felfedezés alapvetően változtatta meg azt, ahogyan a Holdra tekintünk, hiszen kiderült, hogy a Föld kísérője nem egyedülálló jelenség. A 17. század folyamán a csillagászok a Szaturnusz körül is újabb holdakat fedeztek fel, a következő évszázadokban pedig egyre több bolygóról derült ki, hogy saját kísérői vannak. Ezekre az újonnan felfedezett égitestekre végül ugyanazt a szót kezdték használni, amit addig a Föld Holdjára, csak éppen köznévként. Angolul moon lett a nevük, ahogy magyarul is holdaknak nevezzük őket. Amíg egyetlen Holdat ismertünk, azt nem kellett megkülönböztetni semmitől. Amikor viszont egyre több hasonló égitestet fedeztek fel, már szükség volt külön nevekre. Ezek jelentős része a görög és római mitológiából érkezett. Így kapta például a Jupiter négy nagy holdja az Io, Europa, Ganymedes és Callisto nevet. A magyar nyelvben van még egy csavar a történetben, mert nálunk maga a hold szó sem ugyanonnan ered, mint az angol moon. Az ELTE Nyelvtudományi Kutatóközpont Új magyar etimológiai szótára szerint a hold származékszó, ami a hó főnévből keletkezett a -d kicsinyítő képzővel. Itt azonban nem a hónap rövidítéseként ma is használt hó szóról van szó, hanem egy másik, a fehérséghez, világos színhez kapcsolódó hó főnévről. A magyar elnevezés tehát valószínűleg sokkal inkább abból indul ki, amit az ember az égre nézve látott: egy világos, fehéres égitestet a sötét háttér előtt. Ugyanerre az eredetre vezetheti vissza a szótár a régi hóda szót is, ami a szárcsát jelentette. Ennek magyarázata szintén a látvány lehetett, ugyanis a szárcsa csőrének és homlokának egy része fehér. Hasonló szemlélet jelenik meg a hóka szóban is. Maga a hold nagyon régi eleme a magyar nyelvnek. Az etimológiai szótár már 1211-ből felsorol egy bizonytalan, személynévi előfordulást Holdus, illetve Huldus alakban, a 14. századból pedig már olyan említések is vannak, amik a Föld égi kísérőjére utalnak. Az 1372 után keletkezett Jókai-kódexben már a ma is könnyen felismerhető hold alak szerepel. A szó később más jelentéseket is felvett: a 16. század elején például az állatok homlokán található fehér foltot is jelenthette, ami megint csak szépen visszavezet a fehérséghez. Az angol és a magyar szó így két egészen különböző dolgot őrzött meg ugyanarról az égitestről. Az angol moon kifejezés történetében a Hold szabályos ciklusa és az idő mérése maradt meg, míg a magyar Hold esetében valószínűleg az lehetett meghatározó, hogyan nézett ki az éjszakai égbolton. Végül viszont mindkét nyelv ugyanoda jutott. Amikor ezeket a szavakat használni kezdték, még senkinek nem kellett hozzátennie, hogy pontosan melyik holdról beszél. Mire pedig kiderült, hogy a Naprendszer tele van velük, a miénknek már régóta volt neve. Annyira kézenfekvő neve, hogy ma már inkább az összes többit kell külön elneveznünk. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text: Doomsday preacher Paul Mackenzie during a court session of his murder trial judgment at the Mombasa law courts, Kenya on Monday. Photograph: EPA View image in fullscreen Doomsday preacher Paul Mackenzie during a court session of his murder trial judgment at the Mombasa law courts, Kenya on Monday. Photograph: EPA Kenya Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of murder of 190 children and one adult Paul Mackenzie and his church set up sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children, say prosecutors Reuters Mon 19 Oct 2026 12.08 EDT Last modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 12.17 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Kenyan court has found the starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of ⁠190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult-related disasters in recent history. Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast ⁠in south-eastern Kenya. Prosecutors say Mackenzie and ⁠his Good News International Church organised ​a Christian doomsday sect in which they ordered followers to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended. Mackenzie denied murder charges, saying he did not force the victims to starve but the ⁠court rejected that argument. In total, more than 400 bodies have been recovered from the Shakahola forest. Many were severely decomposed, and only 26 of them were able to be identified. Monday’s judgment covered 191 deaths while investigations into the other deaths are continuing. Justice Diana Kavedza Mochache said in a hearing lasting more than eight hours that in some cases children were isolated and denied food while their parents watched. View image in fullscreen Kenyan high court judge Diana Kavedza Mochache on 19 October. Photograph: EPA Mackenzie was in ​court, wearing a striped polo shirt and red trousers, sitting alongside his wife, ‌one of the co-accused. He was silent, ‌staring into space before the ruling was handed down. Relatives of some of those who died in the forest gathered to hear the judgment at Mombasa high ‌court. Francis Wanje, 62, lost eight family members including two grandchildren to the cult. Speaking before the verdict, he said: “It has been really a heavy thing [for] us as a family, and it has really taken us very far in terms of psychological problems … I was hoping for this particular day.” The Shakahola tragedy has gripped Kenya since the discovery of mass graves in the coastal forest more than three years ago. It raised questions over how Mackenzie was able to continue to operate despite having been on the radar of the authorities since 2017 when his premises were searched by police. In 2019, authorities shut down Mackenzie’s church and he relocated ‌to the Shakahola forest, police said. View image in fullscreen A Kenyan national youth service officer talks to a woman while on guard at the entrance to the Mombasa law courts on Monday 19 October. Photograph: Simon Maina/AFP/Getty Images The case has also led to calls for tougher oversight of churches and other religious organisations in a country where religious faith plays a prominent role in public life. Kenya’s president, William Ruto, said in 2023 that government agencies should have been ​able to prevent the deaths. He said he took responsibility as president. People with direct knowledge of the cult’s activities said Mackenzie planned the mass starvation in three phases: first children, then women and young men, and finally the remaining men. Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, forbade cult members from sending their children to school and from going to hospital when they were ill, describing such institutions as satanic, some of his followers told Reuters for a 2023 article. Cult members lived in makeshift homes of polythene ⁠sheeting and thatch that Mackenzie divided into areas with biblical names such as Jerusalem and Judea. View image in fullscreen Paul Mackenzie and his co-accused during their court appearance on 19 October. Photograph: Simon Maina/AFP/Getty Images The plight of his followers began ​to emerge in mid-March 2023, when a local man told ​police that his brother and wife had starved their children ​to death in the forest on Mackenzie’s orders. Mackenzie was arrested but released on bail, after which relatives say he brought forward the date ​on which he told his followers the ‌world would end. Police ​arrested him again in April 2023 and ​started combing through the forest more systematically and began exhuming mass graves. Mackenzie faces other charges over the forest deaths including terrorism-related ones , which he has denied. Prosecutors say while he was in detention he also directed the deaths of 52 people in Kwa Binzaro village, about 18 miles (30km) from Shakahola. Mackenzie has pleaded not guilty in that case.
